Lessons.Title: Finding Limits: Numerical and Graphical Approaches
ExplanationParagraphs: A limit describes approached function value as x approaches a point, whether or not f(a) is defined.
Numerical tables near a from left/right estimate a limit, but require mathematical corroboration.
A two-sided limit exists only if finite one-sided limits agree.
A removable hole can have a finite limit even when function is undefined.
Infinite limits describe unbounded behavior rather than a finite real number.
Independent Cool-down: evaluate a representative local example and explain the limiting or derivative reasoning.

CommonMistakes.WhyWrong: Limit concerns nearby behavior, not isolated point value.
